text_fidelity_a:
ASUS Chromebook C425 Clamshell Laptop, 14" FHD 4-Way NanoEdge, Intel Core m3-8100Y Processor, 8GB RAM, 64GB eMMC Storage, Backlit KB, Silver, Chrome OS, C425TA-DH384 First off this works perfectly for what I wanted it for... sitting on the couch, relaxing, while the TV is on. I do not use this for work or gaming, I have a desktop for that. I was using a tablet, but honestly I hate it. I just can't adjust to typing on a touch screen, I want a real keyboard. I also hate fingerprints on my screen. I deal with it on my phone, but for a larger screen it makes me crazy. So I figured this would be a good solution, when it popped up for review. It fits comfortably on my lap and the screen is small enough I can see over it to watch tv, but large enough it is easy on my eyes. So far its been great, although I miss the left and right mouse buttons built into the touch pad area of most laptops. Maybe its a Chromebook thing, but I will just have to adjust.

I will say though it does feel a bit flimsy. I like the lightness, but in my lap typing I can feel the plastic body flexing. For the price I'd expect something a bit more durable, at least for the bottom half with the keyboard. The keys are responsive, although I'm use to my mechanical keyboard so switching to the thin chiclet style makes them feel mushier than they probably are. For a small laptop, they don't feel cramped and they are raised enough that I'm not miss-typing.

It was incredibly easy to set up, just entered my google log-in info and poof I was up and running. This would be a 5 star product if they hadn't just made it a bit sturdier.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS Chromebook C425 Clamshell Laptop, 14" FHD 4-Way NanoEdge, Intel Core m3-8100Y Processor, 8GB RAM, 64GB eMMC Storage, Backlit KB, Silver, Chrome OS, C425TA-DH384

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Orbit® Fusion™ Wireless Trackball (K72363WW), Black I used a Logitech M570, a thumb trackball, for years until I started gaming again and needed a gaming mouse. Now I’m done with gaming for a while and have been searching for a trackball to reduce strain.

The Kensington Orbit Fusion Wireless Trackball is the first Kensington trackball I’ve tried.

I hate the scroll ring. I think this is either a feature you love or hate, and well, I just don’t like it. Using the scroll ring is uncomfortable for me; I keep going back to my laptop trackpad instead of using it. It’s too easy to move the trackball while using the scroll ring, and I couldn’t decide which finger was most comfortable for using it. I spent a lot of time fiddling with the scrolling speed in the KensingtonWorks program, but content doesn’t move smoothly on my screen -- it jumps.

The mouse is too big for my hand. I usually wear a size small in women’s winter and nitrile gloves, to give an idea of the size. My fingers have to stretch too much to reach the left and right click buttons at the same time. My hand rises off the mouse when I use the scroll ring.

I know some of this is muscle memory, but my wrist and hand actually hurt after using the trackball for more than a few minutes.

I do like that KensingtonWorks can be used on Windows or Mac. I’ve tried a lot of high end gaming mice that I can’t always customize on my Mac. KensingtonWorks lets you modify the pointer, scroll ring, and customize the buttons. You can also back up your settings to Google Drive or Microsoft OneDrive, and set options for specific programs. Kensington also included a USB-A to USB-C adapter.
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Orbit® Fusion™ Wireless Trackball (K72363WW), Black

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express | Easy High Definition (HD) Streaming Media Player (2018) I received this Roku Express for review, but honestly, I just now installed it and I can't tell any difference between it and my previous Roku Express I got about a year and a half ago. It streams exactly the same as far as I can tell, but it streams very well. It was a bit of a pain to install since the Roku site refused my password and the instructions afterwards aren't all that easy to follow if you lose your password. But, after plugging in all my passwords for internet connection, Netflix, Amazon, etc...it finally started streaming again. I can't tell that it's any faster. Nonetheless, if you don't have a Roku and want to stream a boatload of free channels with movies and lots of other cool stuff to watch, I suggest getting a Roku. You can add paid channels later. And Roku doesn't require a credit card to use.

It comes with a short HDMI cable and everything you need to get streaming. As far as the actual hardware installation, it's extremely easy. It takes less than 10 seconds to put it on top of the TV and connect the 2 cables (HDMI and power). A sticky tape comes to adhere the Roku to the top of the TV since the Roku is so small it tends to fall off with being stuck. This is my 3rd Roku and we rarely watch regular TV anymore.
This Roku will stream in 1080 and 720 psi. I had ordered about 5 or so generic Roku remotes earlier this year since we tend to lose them and one of our dogs has chewed up the original remotes beyond usage, and they all work fine with this Roku.

Roku is always good, just a little bit of a pain to get past all the passwords, codes and stuff in the beginning, especially if your old password for some reason doesn't work anymore.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Express | Easy High Definition (HD) Streaming Media Player (2018)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount This TV makes me feel bad for ever having given another product 5 stars. It is really just about perfect. Instead of wasting a lot of space talking about the quality of the picture (believe me, it is there), I am going to concentrate on some finer points, particularly those real and perceived weak points:

(This is replacing a 2009 Sony Z-Series TV, which I also love and still consider a fantastic TV; it was the first year of Internet-capable TVs if I remember correctly, and I used the DLNA features with Universal Media Server, but could never get a Plex profile to work right, so I am happy to have a newer TV that supports Plex via App, besides for the 4k, HDR, etc., etc. I have a bunch of other TVs scattered about, but the other two I use most are less expensive Samsung Smart models from five or so years ago.)

Back to (possible) negatives:

I wasn't sure I would like the stand and style. I always hated those Samsung TVs with the plastic grey legs, and I thought this would look too much like that. I thought my ideal stand was either a perfect 90-degree version of the Sony A1E, or perhaps the A8F, which I had my eye on due to its very low profile, minimalist stand. Anyway, this one looks so much better in real life than I expected. It's actually metal, and fairly dark. Placed on low furniture, it looks great walking by, and sits at the right height while watching. I guess it is made to fit a Sony sound bar perfectly (I use full surround setup, so I don't care). But I am much, much happier with the looks than I thought I would be. If that is your hesitation, go check it out in a store (before coming back for the right price).

Thickness: its thicker than some, including last year's 930E, but the way it angles out from the back gives a much sleeker appearance than you may expect just from looking at the dimensions. You only see its thickness at about 80 degrees to the side. Overall, it sits back far and takes up little extra room than it has to. The TV looks as great off as it does on.

I read a professional review that mentioned the picture doesn't look as good from a side angle. I guess that's true, but it's not nearly as drastic of a change as it sounded from the review. In fact, one of the best TV seats in my house is about 30-degrees off-center, and I don't see a difference from there at all. At 45-degrees, you start to see a difference.

Above mentioned professional review also mentioned the Android TV thing can be a little clunky. I don't feel it, to be honest. It's been nothing but good surprises for me. One thing that could be improved is customization of your home screen. You can re-order some apps, but I haven't figured out how to delete the shortcuts for stuff that isn't even downloaded. And I'm never going to play goofy games on my TV (besides real video games), so how can I get rid of that whole section that is taking up space. You can block recommended content, so after them pushing some crapware on you initially, you can basically run add-free. Looks like you'll probably have to sign in to Google, though, but you can make a new account just for your TV (which is what I do for every device).

The downward facing ports look really good with the cable management, so good that I really don't want to use any of the side inputs for permanent setups. For that reason, they should have put the IR blaster and composite input facing down as well (not that I need them, as I don't have cable, but some people will).

Not that I even checked my link speed, but manual says Ethernet port is 100mbps. Can't imagine you'll ever need more than that unless you expect to run uncompressed video without a converter.

The remote is nicer than I expected, but still not as nice as my old one. Plus, although it has Bravia Sync, it doesn't easily just control my stereo the way I would like it to (as my old Sony TV did).Not sure why there has to be a Google button on the remote. Or even Netflix. These should be programmable. Actually, four programmable Apps and/or Input buttons would be greatly appreciated in their place.

That's about it for nitpicking. Here's some things that are totally awesome (besides all the obvious):

It can read all commonly used containers for video files, including *mkv, and it can decompress 4k HEVC (H.265) video natively. So even though my NAS cannot transcode 4k on the fly, if I set it to run at full quality, the TV does it just fine! And since H.265 was made because of 4k video, here's hoping we don't have formats this TV can't play any time soon. This is just fantastic to me, as I really love my NAS' Plex server function. You can also play up to 4k H.265 video right off a hard drive via USB.

My UMS media server is showing up under Video devices (which is where the DLNA servers show up), but you can't see the files. I haven't messed with it much (because now I don't care), but I assume they'll get a profile working before long.

I love the built-in TV guide function and also the way you can browse other channels along the bottom of your screen without changing the channel. These are both great features (the TV guide function on my old TV was abandoned after a few years, but I expect this one will continue to operate). I do not have or want cable, so now I have the features that are nice to have with cable without the burden of slow response cable boxes and the burden of dealing with Comcast.

I haven't even tried out the professional settings (or even messed with anything but motionflow) because the TV is impressing me every second it's on. Again, as this is the first 4k TV to reside in my house, I guess I should be amazed. But the blacks as bars on movies wider than 16:9 are so black you don't notice them. Space scenes are to die for. 4k is done right here: this is the high end of quality, about the only thing worth removing my old Z-series for. I just love it. It looks amazing on and off, and does everything I want it to do (mainly Plex, and Netflix is nice now and then as well). I'm so happy that Plex works so well with this TV without an expensive NAS upgrade, even with movies encoded at 2160p and 7.1 surround. Just fantastic.

It's better than I expected even from Sony's almost-second-to-flagship model. About as high end as they come before they jump up drastically in price. I wouldn't have anything less on my primary TV stand, and I don't need anything more. Highly recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Sony XBR65X900F 65-Inch 4K Ultra HD Smart LED TV with $40 Off TV Wall Mount

text_fidelity_a:
Hosa CMP-105 1/4" TS to 3.5 mm TRS Mono Interconnect Cable, 5 Feet There are many ways one could review this product. I am choosing to give an example of how my family used it. It is a great, functional cable with many other possible uses as well.

After an attempt to use [[ASIN:B005INJ4ZG My Zone Wireless Headphones]] was a bust for me due to its terrible sound quality, my techie husband bought this cable for me as part of a setup that allows me to listen to TV as loud as I want without disturbing him or the neighbors.

I directly hook up this [[ASIN:B000KIPT30 amp]] to a head phone or earbuds when I am sitting close to the TV by using a special [[ASIN:B00009UVPN adapter]]. Head phones and earbuds have a 1/8 inch (3.5 mm) male jack (AKA male connector). Without an adapter, they can't be inserted into this amp, whose plug (AKA socket, female jack, or female connector) measures 1/4 inch (6.35 mm).

Because I like to move around my living room when I am watching TV, my husband also bought me a special [[ASIN:B0010CX798 male-to-female, headphone adapter, extension cable]]. The 1/4-inch, male jack of this cable fits into the 1/4-inch plug of this amp, and it has a 1/8-inch plug on its other end into which the jack of a head phone or ear bud can fit.

In order to use this setup, my husband also hooked into the amp this particular male-to-male extension cable. As you can see, one end is 1/8-inch and the other is 1/4-inch in diameter. The smaller end fits into a plug on the TV. When I want to use this external speaker source, I use the TV remote to access a menu that allows me to do that. Once this system is hooked up, I can no longer adjust the sound volume on the TV itself. I use the volume control on this amp.

Note that there is no On/Off switch on the particular amp we used. If you want to turn it off, so that you are not wasting electricity when it is not in use, you unhook the power cord from the far-left side of the amp.

This setup is a little complicated for the non-techie to figure out on their own, but if you have anyone techie in your family who can do it for you, it works really well.
text_fidelity_b: Hosa CMP-105 1/4" TS to 3.5 mm TRS Mono Interconnect Cable, 5 Feet

APC Back-UPS Pro 1000VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BR1000G) I got this for Christmas and have only been using it for a few days now. I did have a problem with the set-up since there were no step by step instructions and you are left to figure out what goes where. I had omitted attaching the USB/phone jack between my old Windows XP computer and the UPS. I've used UPS's in years past, but they did not require a USB connection to a computer. I found out I had a problem when I was trying to install the software and it stopped loading and gave me a problem message, but no solution. I called the 1-888 number and without any fuss or waiting I got to speak to someone in the tech department who spoke very good English and solved my problem quickly.

I was tempted to deduct one star for the lousy (or total lack of) any instructions on how to connect this to your computer but didn't since the tech help was so good. There was a picture drawing instructing the user to remove the battery and turn it over so the green tape is on top which I managed to do alright. I don't hear any fan noise whatsoever as some others were complaining of. In fact, it's so quiet I can't even tell it's on unless I go and see the 3 LED lights on the top panel.

I tested it out a few minutes ago by turning off the power to the room that my computer is in. I was downstairs in the garage at the fuse box so I don't know if any beep occurred upstairs, but when I got there the computer was running off the UPS. Every 30 seconds I heard 4 beeps from the UPS telling me that it was being used as the power source. I only have my computer, monitor and modem connected to the UPS. I figure I don't need the extra peripheral equipment to stay powered up since it only sucks more energy from my UPS. I didn't wait to see how long the UPS would power my PC but I did sit there for about 3 minutes before I went downstairs and turned the power back on. My computer had a message on the screen saying that it was now being powered by regular current again (or something to that effect).

So far I like this UPS a LOT. There's nothing more frustrating then losing your work if the power goes off for only a couple of seconds. I edit a lot of music and it's not always easy or convenient to save it while I edit it just because of the nature of the program I use. So, I really like the idea of hearing my 4 beeps to let me know I might need to close out and shut down and not lose any work. I don't always have lights on so there may be nothing to tell me there's been a power outage except for the beeps on this UPS. There is a mute mode, but I need to hear the beeps.
text_fidelity_b: APC Back-UPS Pro 1000VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BR1000G)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player Picture is nice,

The real reason I'm sending the units (I've had two) back, however, is that the player refuses to output the various high quality audio formats, including 7.1 DTS Master Audio. The digital coax cable barely works and the HDMI 2 audio output simply does not work, Admittedly I have an older receiver -- a Sony STR-DA5400ES, from 2009. But it has multiple HDMI inputs and the HDMI 2 audio output on the X800 is specifically designed to send audio to an older amp. Even Sony phone support says it should work. But it doesn't.. I spent 1 hour and 7 minutes with Sony ES support today going through every possible menu permutation on both the Amp and the UBP-X800 player. No luck The HDMI is dead. Zero output. The coax output can only send DTS EX 5.1, even though the player itself tells me it's playing DTS Master Audio 7.1.

This UBP-X800 has two HDMI outputs: one for video, one for audio. In case you don't have a 4K receiver with the ever-changing HDMI protocols, you're supposed to be able to feed HDMI audio to the amp. So I fed the video directly to the Samsung's video input (a direct cable connection) and another HDMI to my amp.

Zero audio from the player's HDMI audio feed. Not a peep of audio at all.

So I used the orange RCA digital audio coax connector to get surround sound audio.

But the coax digital audio cable only delivers DTS EX 5.1, not the 7.1 DTS Master Audio available on the Kingsman 4K disk. I updated the player's and the TV's firmware and read the manual. Nothing fixes the problem. Using all new, very short, high-speed HDMI 2.0 cables too.

My ancient Sony BDP-S560 Blu-ray player feeds all formats to the same 5400ES amp properly. I get great 7.1 DTS Master HD audio. Thus my old Blu-ray player sounds way better than my brand new advanced Sony UHD player.
Researching at the Sony forum under the UBP-X800 Audio Problems thread, answers were all over the place and none worked, I tried to register so I could post my problem and the website wouldn't allow me to. The comments there were complaining that they could not get the ATMOS tracks working.

I have no choice but to pack both X800s up and send them back.

Eventually I found that I needed to plug the 4K player into input 3 of the TV for the image to stabilize. Interesting that only some inputs on the TV can handle UHD source. But still, the player's audio doesn't work with my Sony Amp (Sony's fault).

HDMI was supposed to solve all these problems, but I suspect the HDCP copy protection schemes are really screwing things up or the firmware has bugs or companies just produce inferior products. Rather disappointing.
text_fidelity_b: Sony UBP-X800 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray Player

Klipsch GiG Black Portable Speaker, Black I really wanted to like this speaker. It comes complete with international plugs, an a/c wall charger, and two pouches which I assume is one for the unit and one for the accessories. It is somewhat attractive with a built-in stand that allows you to either place it on its side or in an upright position.

With most speakers, once you have paired it with your device (an Iphone 5s, in my case), you should be all done. This is not so with this unit. The speaker has a spring-loaded slide switch that you push on. It gives you a guitar confirmation tone so that you know that it's working. Now you must go to the "Settings" icon on your device and manually choose the Klipsch speaker. Then you will hear another guitar confirmation tone letting you know that it is paired. You must do this EVERY SINGLE TIME. It is ridiculous. Of course when you turn it off, it will give you yet another guitar confirmation tone.

The sound is very good, but the extra step of always having to re-enable the bluetooth connection through "Settings" totally negates anything positive about this speaker. There is absolutely no reason why my Sony SRSX5 and my JBL Charge automatically pair with my device whenever I turn them on, and yet this one does not. I keep trying to understand why the developers came up with this procedure, but it totally baffles me.

I know that other users have complained in the past about charging issues. Perhaps Klipsch listened to them and fixed this problem because I have not had any difficulties with that.

If you're gonna spend money on a good speaker, please look at the Sony SRSX5. It is an outstanding speaker with logical functions and exceptional sound.
text_fidelity_b: Klipsch GiG Black Portable Speaker, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Dropcam Pro indoor Wi-Fi Wireless Video Monitoring Security Camera 720p There are a lot of problems with Nest/Dropcam. Some of the problems are:

1) Dropcam was purchased by Google not too long ago. Google is a massive company with ample resources but they are completely reluctant to invest in this company to make it a good buy for customers.

2) They have very inexperienced people for tech support and you will spend hours on the phone. Ultimately, you will get nowhere because the technical problems are inherent to their system.

3) You must rely on ISP-provided bandwidth and the ISP providers are cheating us out of the bandwidth we pay for, (I found this with Verizon and Frontier) so the cameras don't work well. Google needs to own a bandwidth company and provide enough levels and packages of bandwidth for its Dropcam customers to allow multiple cameras to work well. If you only need one camera, then possibly this system might work for you if you only need very basic services. Otherwise, the lack of enough bandwidth and the photo array display will cause immediate problems.

4) When I got my first Dropcam camera, I was told that I would be billed ten dollars a year for the first camera and half that for each subsequent camera. These prices are now monthly.

5) You get thumbnail individual shots for the recorded history (not video streaming film). Because the individual pictures are taken at intervals, they do not always report what is going on. Recently, there were eight people in a cottage on my property. The intermittent pictures did not contain even ONE shot of all of those eight people having been there. I have had this system for several years and I have not been able to capture even one picture of the people who have been repeatedly burglarizing my home and the cottage.

6) The thumbnail pictures are too small and difficult to review and the quality is poor. Details are often lost; like the features on a person's face. If you try and call it up into the larger screen, it will not give you the picture you are trying to review; it will give you a "stock" picture of the room minus the people you are trying to see.

7) The cameras are not a high quality. They respond in bizarre ways to the light at different times of the day. The cameras are supposed to report in color; the thumbnail pictures from the array only report in black and white. Often the cameras only report an almost black room.

7) I have written Dropcam/Nest multiple times. I have complained on the phone multiple times. They are unresponsive for all their talk. If you can find another company, I suggest you do so. This company is being poorly run and is customer unfriendly where corrections or upgrades to their system are concerned. They are primarily interested in providing things to the customer that they can charge for; they are not interested in whether or not those things run well and deliver the goods.

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher Price Precious Planet Whale of a Tub We purchased this product before we were expecting, knowing that it was neutral gendered and would be perfect for a boy or a girl. When we had our first child, a 9 lb, 11 oz baby girl, I was SO nervous! I didn't know a thing about babies. My eldest sister helped me give her her first bath and complimented our whale tub. She said it was so nice that the green padding in the base would help prevent baby from slipping. By the third bath, I had it down.

As the weeks have gone on, our little one has really loved her tub. She began holding her head up at 4 days old and was doing so independently within a month of her birth. She loved kicking and splashing in her tub. She has never cried in the bath. We use a turtlemeter thermometer and she thinks of it like a little toy with which to play.

I would recommend this tub with the seat in it for a newborn baby up to about 12 lbs. Once our daughter was 13 lbs, she has trouble staying warm in the tub with the seat attached. It simply wasn't deep enough for her while she was lying down and she only got her bottom half wet unless I poured water over her, and the chilly air would then make her cold.

With the seat out, she needs to be sitting on her own so there was a two month gap where we did not use her tub, and instead bathed her with me in the big tub.

Once she was a successful sitter, we returned her to this tub for warmer nights, so she could sit and play in the water. She loves it!

After a bath, I would recommend not only using the drain in the tub, but turning this whale tub upside-down and and then turning it from side-to-side to drain it, as the water tends to get trapped beneath the green padded area. You can also remove the seat to clean under it. Using dish soap and a scrub daddy sponge, I am able to quickly clean the tub in-between uses.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher Price Precious Planet Whale of a Tub

text_fidelity_a: AMORNO Bluetooth Headphones, Foldable Wireless Neckband Headset with Retractable Earbuds, Sports Sweatproof Noise Cancelling Stereo Earphones with Mic (Grey) True story.. I go through headphones like they are disposable cups.. Honestly this year alone I have bought 14 pairs of headphones.. both neckband and true wireless ones.. I listen to podcasts all day everyday. I always have a headphone in.. I fall asleep with them listening to Synctuition and I listen to a podcast when I wake up for work. The second I'm out of the shower, an earbud goes in.. I have one pair charging at all times so I'm never without.. Being used heavily.. the bands break, the cords breaks, one bud stops working, one bud goes missing, the Bluetooth stops working, the microphone stops working.. the list goes on.. I probably should just buy an expensive pair but honestly I'm convinced I'll just break or lose them.. So I stick with affordable ones until I inevitably break or lose them.. I tell you this to reassure you that I KNOW my headphones.. These have been great so far. The battery on them is killer. I can get two whole days of literal continuous use before the dreaded "battery low" warning. They retract really quickly and smoothly. They are light weight and the sound is great. I will say though, that I am not qualified to judge sound quality.. I usually only have one bud in at a time to be able to drive, work, talk to others and since it's mostly podcasts.. I can't say that the bass is amazing or the treble is whatever.. I do listen to both at night to sleep music and they sound great but again.. not my forte. Endurance and battery life are though and so far these have far surpassed the usual time when I need to replace them.. Great buy for a great price.
text_fidelity_b: AMORNO Bluetooth Headphones, Foldable Wireless Neckband Headset with Retractable Earbuds, Sports Sweatproof Noise Cancelling Stereo Earphones with Mic (Grey)

text_fidelity_a: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone - Matte Black (Old Model) These headphones do have a more balanced sound than the horrible original Beats that were just too bass heavy. The Bluetooth pairing was quick and easy and battery life is decent. The case and accessories seem to be good quality. In all honesty though for the sound quality I'd never pay the retail asking price for these or recommend them to anyone. I got a used pair (yes they are real Beats) for half the price of new and at this price point I feel it's worth it. The noise canceling isn't anything to write home about and if it's a big reason why you're considering these I'd look to Bose or elsewhere where it's done much better. Another point with these is comfort. They're ok for an hour or so, but I'd not want these on pushing two or more. They tend to pinch at the ear cup level and you can see in various pics how the cups nearly touch when not on the head. So the farther you are pushing those cups out the more they are fighting to close so to speak. I don't have a large head, I don't expand the headband at all when wearing, and they get a little clampy after a bit. Another comfort issue is the interior depth of the ear cups. I don't have big ear or ones that stick out and I still feel my ears slightly pushing against the speaker. I couldn't imagine anyone with large ears being happy with these at all and if you fall into that category I'd definitely try on a pair in a store before buying. The cup pads are nice and it's too bad they didn't make them just a tad deeper.  So in summary these are good headphones if not great ones, but honestly not worth retail. The Bluetooth is nice, but you're obviously paying for image here.

text_fidelity_a:
Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging One of the most important attributes for a headset is comfort. I've tried a few over the years, but always have found them to be a pain (literally!) if they are worn for more than 20 minutes or so. I'm very happy to report that the Moto is a dream when it comes to comfort - had it on for a three+ hour drive, and didn't even know it was there. Plus, it didn't cause a problem with my glasses, unlike other models I've tried.

Set up was very straightforward - basically just follow the prompts and it works. I didn't try out the text-to-voice feature but it sounds interesting. Not really something I would use since I don't text much at all, but if you're text-heavy, that feature would certainly be of value.

Audio quality was excellent. Had no problems hearing callers even with music playing in the car. Range was also very good.

My complaints are two-fold. First a minor one - this comes packed in what I would consider to be wasteful packaging. Looks impressive in a clear, thick plastic box, but the amount of materials used for packing is unnecessary. I did not, however, deduct anything from its rating due to that.

What did cause a loss of one star was the mic pickup. In a quiet environment it was fine. But, in a noisy environment (such as outside, in a crowded restaurant or with moderate-level music playing in the car), it picks up so much background noise that people had problems hearing me. To ensure this was actually the case, I loaned it to a friend and had him call me so I could hear for myself. It seems that the mic is either way too sensitive or not sufficiently directional - it truly is hard to hear the person's voice when they are using the headset should they be in anything other than a pretty quiet environment..

But, that aside, this is the best headset I've used to date. Especially recommended if you have had comfort issues with other headsets or are a glasses wearer.
text_fidelity_b: Motorola CommandOne Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
RCA RCRPS06GR 6 Device Universal Remote What occurred to me after wasting half an hour with this thing is that what is needed is an iPhone app to control your television and stereo, not a single freaking light bulb and a long, long list of codes printed in mouse type.

See photo. The remote looks good, shiny Darth Vader black. There are three manuals, one of which is about an ounce and a half. One is a long list of codes and the third unfolds to about 10x17 so that between the three differently-sized printed manuals you have a lap full of clutter which is difficult to manage while you're trying to press buttons in some order.

I couldn't get it to do much of anything, and by the time I realized that half an hour had gone by and I was getting hot under the collar, I thought: FAIL. Why waste any more of my time? Ah, but by THAT time I was and am good and frustrated at this RCA product. RCA. Who knew they were still in business? Who the heck would buy an RCA product? I'm sure they made great gramophones back in the day, but Sony came by and ate their lunch and even that was forty years ago.

If you were an RCA exec, wouldn't you want to make certain that anything your company made was functional? I've got a couple college degrees. I can tie my own shoes. I can do all kinds of things, but I couldn't figure out how to program this little (EXPLETIVE DELETED) thing. Which frustrates me.

The first thing I noticed (after I cut the I-dare-you-to-open-me hard plastic packaging) was that it hurt to open the battery compartment. There's some idiotic L-shaped trigger you have to depress, meaning that you're digging it under your fingernails, which I think most people would find painful. Just a dumb design move. No other word for it. Dumb.

The remote looks good and has some interesting ribs underneath it. The buttons are not what you might expect, the volume and channel buttons are flabby feeling and weak, not definite-feeling. The center "OK" button is kind of clicky, like cellophane. There's a whole array of buttons, but it's not worth my time to try and program each one. And I grew to dislike the hard plastic feeling of the remote. There are other plastic materials that feel better to the hand. LOOK AT SONY PRODUCTS, RCA, LOOK AT SONY PRODUCTS FOR A FREE CLUE.

I'm annoyed and frustrated. This seemed like such a neat idea. But sitting on my couch juggling three differently-sized manuals AND this remote and wondering why none of these instructions were doing anything was really frustrating, just not how I want to spend my free time. I'll happily continue to exist with my TV remote, my surround-sound remote, my AppleTV remote and the AT&T cable box remote, you know? BECAUSE THEY WORK and they work without frustrating me.

Here's my idea: RCA hires an app developer and somehow figures out how to have your devices tell the app what their codes area. Something like that. Because the notion of combing through a manual full of codes in tiny type is worse than doing your income taxes.

THE WORLD HAS MOVED ON, RCA and you are apparently living in the 1970s with burgundy leisure suits and avocado-colored kitchen appliances.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS REMOTE, IT WILL ONLY FRUSTRATE YOU and dig in the skin under your nails. Ouch. Did this thing really have to be so frustrating? Do you imagine this is the kind of experience consumers are after? Not just one more freaking remote control, but one that promises convenience and delivers frustration? Not a good product. Stay away from it.
text_fidelity_b: RCA RCRPS06GR 6 Device Universal Remote

text_fidelity_a:
Lexar JumpDrive S73 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive LJDS73-64GASBNA (Green) I'm not going to bother with a detailed listing of times as many other reviewers have done a nice job with that. I'll just say that I did time out this device in comparison to a pair of my 2.0 flashdrives and another 3.0 on a pair of Macs, one with 2.0 USB and one with 3.0 USB. There's no doubt it's speedier in all cases than my 2.0s, whether I was transferring over a folder with a lot of docs or a folder with mixed media (docs, photos, video). Roughly 2-3 times as fast than 2.0 consistently (that's with both of them in the 2.0 ports), though the gap narrowed with really large, mixed folders. When it goes into the 3.0, it was consistently 3-4 times faster, with again a narrower gap with really large, mixed files. In comparison to a Triton, it was definitely significantly and noticeably slower, a little bit better than half as fast.

The device feels very light and the casing not quite as sturdy as my other drives, though I never feel like it's in danger of breaking. Just doesn't have the same sense of heft and durability.

On the other hand, the slide clicks in nicely and solid, with a satisfying sound and doesn't retract easily unless you are wanting it to

If you have a 2.0 drive, it'll be noticeably faster and if you're looking for a drive, makes sense to get one that can go with you to your next upgrade. If you've upgraded to 3.0 and want a new drive just for that, there's no doubt you'll notice the difference, and especially with large files and movies etc. I'd ay it's definitely worth it. As for going beyond to the Triton, personally my need for speed isn't that great--this one would suit me fine. Some people though have less patience than I do. Plus, I'm cheap. So slower than the other 3.0, but I'd say still a fine value.
text_fidelity_b: Lexar JumpDrive S73 64GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive LJDS73-64GASBNA (Green)

Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging The frustration free packaging is a big plus.
The mount itself is perfect for our needs.
We have a Garmin Nuvi which came with the window suction mount. The window mount has a ball-joint the same as this friction mount.
The GPS came with the clip-on bracket which has the socket attached which then clips onto the ball on this friction mount.
This forms a multi-directional ball and socket joint allowing for easy angle adjustments.

This mount has stayed in place with no problems, even when we've armorall'ed the dashboard. Then again, we don't fling the truck around like teenagers either, the worst we do is bounce it around on some dirt roads.

We much prefer this over the window mount for several reasons:
We live in Georgia (USA) and the heat and the humidity in summer takes its toll on the sucker attachments on the window mounts.
For security, we move the GPS from sight whenever we park.... the whole unit is easily picked up and placed on the floor.
We couldn't do this with a window mount. We either unclipped and left the mount attached to the window, a visible tell-tale that there's a GPS in the vehicle. Or, we would fiddle to remove the whole mount from the window (never too easy), and then are left with a tell-tale suction scum ring on the window! ...once more telling would-be GPS thieves that there's a GPS in the car! And that scum ring is just unsightly. Yes, you can get wipes... but this is a far more elegant solution and much more convenient.
Recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
Cisco-Linksys WRT160N Wireless-N Broadband Router I was having terrible problems connecting to work from home over VPN. My MS communicator (IM) and Outlook just wouldn't work right over VPN. The help desk at work blamed by bandwidth and ISP (comcast). This didn't make sense since everyone nearly else at work also uses comcast and has the same bandwidth.

Many folks at work were also having issues with IM and said switching to a Linksys router fixed their isses - so I took the plunge. It did fix my IM. And, the wireless signal strength is better than before.

But, it didn't fix Outlook. Linksys and my IT help folks looked at it. I spent more time rebooting my computer in the past week than I could stand.

Outlook still would not work over my wireless but I could connect with no issues over my neighbors unsecured network. I called Comcast and they wanted to upgrade my modem's software but said the thing was soooo old it had to be replaced. A comcast guy was at my house by later in the day and replaced my modem in less than one hour - half of that on-hold waiting for the tech guy at comcast proper to pick up the phone so they could work together.

Within minutes of the modem being set up I was happily working away over VPN using Outlook and IM and everything else. It's nearly as fast as being in the office. My connection over VPN and not over VPN is clearly faster than before - it's also less prone to drop outs.

Long story short. It's a great router but don't expect it to fix everything. Make sure your modem is the most up to date both in terms of hardware and software too. Basically, any piece of anything between you and your internet could gum up the works and it's hard knowing where the issues is (router, modem, network card, etc.) I can't believe the number of well trained tech people I spoke to and not one of them questioned the modem. All of them seemed to think since I could get to the internet not over VPN that using VPN should make no difference. Clearly it did - apparently older modems don't play well with VPN.
text_fidelity_b: Cisco-Linksys WRT160N Wireless-N Broadband Router

text_fidelity_a:
G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling I've had the opportunity to review three different G.G. Martinsen players, and of the three this one is my favorite. I brought two of the players, pre-charged, to review at my sister's where I am staying a week while she had and recovers from surgery, and the one thing I can say right off the bat is that I wish the charging cable was of the ubiquitous Micro-A type and not the mini type, which I did not think to bring with me. The [[ASIN:B016F4AGLC other player]] handles like the [[ASIN:B0173CW2CQ first one]] I reviewed for G.G. Martinsen, but I will have to wait until I get back home to do anything other than test the recorder and FM radio on this 16GB player because I have no cable to copy music onto the player with!

Anyway, unlike the other two players, the controls on this one make sense and handle more like what I'm used to. The instructions that come with this (that I also left at home!) were well-written in English, unlike so many products coming out of China these days. But I haven't needed the instructions to figure out how to use this player or change the settings. The first thing I did was set the Power Off and Sleep settings to 0 so the player won't shut off unless I flip the manual switch to turn it off. I have been listening to this player while I've been writing reviews, and I have had absolutely no cutouts with the FM radio even though I'm in a condo sandwiched on all sides by other units and this place is bad with reception of cable TV and other radios. I like that the station stays selected even when you power the player off and on again.

The control dial is easy to see, with a top Menu button, left and right arrows, and a pause/play button on the bottom (something the other players did not have). The round button in the middle has a good tactile feel, and even in the dark it's fairly easy to feel where to press for the different functions. I'll have to re-read the instructions to understand fully when to use the center button and how.

The little piece you can thread a lanyard into is plastic, but I don't think it will break easily unless you put a lot of stress on it. The player comes with a pair of original Apple-style earphones, which are great for walking outside where you need to be able to hear sounds around you while listening to music. The headphones are not the best in the world, but they are a nice additional feature and good to have in situations where you wouldn't want pricier headphones to get ruined (the gym, outside should it start raining). Of course, your listening experience will only be as good as the wired headphones you plug into this player. It really is a whole lot of bang for the buck and an attractive little player. I have the turquoise color, and it's really nice.

I put links to the other two players I have reviewed so you can compare them. What I like about this one is it doesn't have that gimmicky bubble-gum type selection screen but, rather, just has a list of the different features and functions. The list is easy to read and looks more businesslike and professional than the more cartoonish screens of the other two players.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling

text_fidelity_a:
Tsir Tech® TT-LD82 Adjustable Wooden Laptop Desk with Built in Cooling Fan Bottom line: this provides a great value for the price. Lots of adjustability, decent construction quality, and nice looks.

Full review: This is a great laptop workstation for when I want to use my laptop while on the sofa but don't want to use my actual lap top to hold it. It also is great for holding a tablet so I can view a video while eating without getting the tablet in harms way of some errant food.

Assembly was straightforward. Basically I just needed to attach the casters, the center pole and the table top. The only fasteners were 4 screws and 2 bolts, so it went together in just a few minutes. A combo allen wrench/phillips screwdriver is included, but I found it much more comfortable to use a regular screwdriver. The instructions were clear and easy to follow.

In addition to being a table, it includes a USB hub which is a very welcome addition. It also has a cooling fan built into the table top (USB powered from a laptop) and a LED light on a stalk (3 AA batteries needed, which are not included).

The table top, when fully extended on the center pole, is 30.5 inches tall; fully retracted it's 22 inches tall. More than enough adjustment room. The table itself is 15 inches by about 22 inches (measurements taken at the widest points). I had no problems using it with a full-size laptop and had enough room left over for using an external mouse.

The table top tilts and can be locked into any angle. It can also be placed in a vertical position to save space when it's being stored. When the top is in a vertical position the entire unit can be easily picked up and moved by using the built-in handle, which I found to be a very nice design feature. I also liked that there is a small cubby under the table top that is useful for storing cables and other small items.

The wheels are small, but I didn't have any problems moving the table back and forth in use on both a medium pile carpet and a hard floor. Only two of the casters have locks, so when assembling it, make sure the wheels with the locks are on different sides to ensure good locking performance.

The build quality is quite nice - far better than I expected given the price. The legs and supports are all metal; the adjustment ring for the table height locks tightly, and the adjustment for the table tilt is easy to use.

The appearance is also quite nice. It looks more like furniture than my old one (which was all beige and looked like it belonged in a hospital). The cherry-colored wood-grained top looks nice against the black legs.

All in all, very pleased with this and would definitely recommend it if you're looking for a laptop table.
[The manufacturer provided the product for review]
text_fidelity_b: Tsir Tech® TT-LD82 Adjustable Wooden Laptop Desk with Built in Cooling Fan

text_fidelity_a:
AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA Ok I can be a bit of a headphone snob, but at a near $300 price point I have some pretty high expectations. I ran them through my standard audio tests and these passed every one with flying colors. Bottomline, where most wireless sets fail is with bass, either its lacking or they overcompensate for it at the expense of everything else. (I'm talking to you SkullCandy). These however managed to be astounding on bass without it being overwhelming. Deep rich sounds, but mid and upper still came in crystal clear. It was impressive.

They also manage to have noise canceling without the annoying hiss present in the high end SkullCandy set I recently reviewed. The AKG's are superior and even performed better than my beloved, but admittedly old Sennheisers. How they would match up against a newer pair I can't say though, I will fangirl all day over a high end set of Senn's, but these AKGs give them some serious competition.

The ambient pass-through was a welcome addition, and these paired effortlessly via blue tooth. The ear cups were comfortable, although warm like every other pair of closed noise-canceling headsets I've tried. I will be honest I tend to prefer an open headset, but that is more preference than anything to do with this set. The ear cups were smaller than other pairs I've worn, I'm petite so that wasn't an issue but if you got yourself some good sized ears keep that in mind.

So if you have $300 burning a hole in your pocket and need some very well balanced wireless headphones, I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA

ASUS ZenPad 3S 10 9.7" (2048x1536), 4GB RAM, 64GB eMMC, 5MP Front / 8MP Rear Camera, Android 6.0, Tablet, Glacier Silver (Z500M-C1-SL) As a long-time Apple user, I am strongly considering other options because of a number of issues, including software updates that slow to a halt older devices ("planned obsolescence" is what they call it). Between that, the higher cost, and a few other things, I'm in the market for a different tablet and computer.

In the past, the problem switching back was that, unlike with Apple, things were not quite as user friendly with the interface and you had to really figure things out instead of it being immediately apparent.

Happily, it was different with this tablet. Out of the box, my family and I were able to figure it out quickly and easily, giving us hope in another option.

Quality: Great image on the screen with very high resolution! The feel of the device is also sturdy, aesthetically pleasing, lightweight, and thin.

User-friendly layout, very accessible, good features, and it works seamlessly with Google. I've got google email and YouTube channels, so it's nice to know there's a trade-off for losing some of the other things like seamless transitions between iTunes, my current calendar (not in love with that--I can just as easily switch to google or droid for this)...

All this adds up to the following: Apple can no longer claim to be the clear leader in tablets, phones, and computers. They have stopped innovating far beyond comparable products, and now, for the value and overall performance, the ZenPad is a worthy adversary.

I still have my MacBook Pro computer, but when it comes time to buy a new one, I will be ready to switch knowing items like these are available.
What a great surprise!

text_fidelity_a:
Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black) I never owned a tablet or a smartphone so I suppose if I did my review might be different but I think this is a pretty neat little tablet and the price is pretty great too.

I've had it for a couple of days and downloaded the Amazon App store which has most of the apps anyone could need. I mean seriously how many apps does an average person really use? I have downloaded quite a few games for both myself and my kids, the Kindle app, I heart Radio app, and the US newspaper app. So far its holding all of it but I also ordered a microsdhc card for extra space to hold more apps and e-books. I have a regular Kindle that I've had for quite a few years and I am able to transfer most of the books onto this tablet also (I haven't tried downloading all of them since my son uses a few for school). It has where you can calibrate the stylus. Also if you longpress the stylus onto the wallpaper it will let you change the wallpaper in the background.

It does not come with a camera and flashplayer is not installed (but what I understand you can install a "lite" version of flashplayer which I have not done as of yet). The touchscreen is more geared toward using the stylus (which is included) which is a let down to some people. You can use your fingertip but it isn't as responsive as with the stylus IMO. It also comes with a sleeve (that has a place for your stylus) and earphones. There is a charger and a USB cable. There is another cable which I'm not sure exactly what its for (sorry). I haven't used the other cables just yet (except the charger of course). As for battery life it does seem like it runs down pretty quickly (perhaps 3-4 hours). Of course, that may change depending on the type of apps you have running. I know a lot of people worry about reading books from this rather than the Kindle type e-ink. I, personally, like reading at night before I go to sleep and with the Kindle I had to keep a lamp on just to see the page..(barely)...whereas this isn't like that (my eyes are much happier!) You can change the brightness of the screen if you are worried about the brightness bothering your eyes.

I have my email accessible to the Coby Kyros so I can check it throughout the day since my daughter takes off with my laptop quite often. I also downloaded the Dolphin mini browser which I like better than the browser sent with the Kyros. It comes with the GetJar app store which has quite a few apps but Amazon has more.

Of course, I cannot guarantee how well it will hold up because I've only had it for a couple of days but overall its a nice simple little tablet. I've seen the reviews of more expensive tablets and I don't want to spend $400 on a tablet that's rated two stars. I was willing to take the chance and so far I'm happy with my purchase. I rated it 4 stars because the speaker is kinda crappy...I haven't tried listening to the radio with earphones...hopefully it sounds better. And also I wish that it was easier to install flash (I've been looking on the internet but it seems like you have to be really a techie to do it...and I'm not!) It's not an Ipad (or Ipod) so you can't rate this tablet against a product like that (of course it's half the price of a Ipod touch).
text_fidelity_b: Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black)

text_fidelity_a: WYZE Cam 1080p HD Indoor Smart Home Camera with Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Compatible with Alexa & the Google Assistant Bulbs and outlet are OK. I would not buy separately though, as nowadays you get higher quality bulbs and outlets for a discount price.  The sensor bridge, contact and motion sensors are problematic to say the least. I have 2 contact sensors and 3 motion sensors connected to the sensor bridge. Right now all of them are offline, they started going offline one by one. Distance from the sensors to the bridge is not an issue since two of them are located no more than three feet away from the bridge. This is not the first time this has happened. The only solution for me has been to reset bridge and sensors, and reinstall them one by one. Many people complain about the same issue, and this keeps happening. The camera where the bridge is attached is installed 7 ft from the ground, so it has been very aggravating to have to get a ladder every time one of these switches has gone offline. Regarding the camera, you probably will not find anything cheaper in the market right now. This model in particular offers continuous recording provided you insert a storage card, that is a plus. Person detection is back, however sometimes it takes more than 10 minutes to receive a notification. Some people has reported that it has take up to one hour to get the notification. I personally would not recommend getting this package due to the unreliability of the bridge and motion and contact sensors. This is definitely not a system you want to buy to secure your home. The camera can be purchased separately for about $25. The video quality is acceptable during the daytime. If you want a hobby camera, you will not find a better deal. For security purposes, you are better off looking somewhere else.

Razer Opus Active Noise Cancelling ANC Wireless Headphones: THX Audio Tuning - 25 Hr Battery - Bluetooth 4.2 & 3.5mm Jack Compatible - Auto Play/Auto Pause - Carrying Case Included - Midnight Blue At first glance, the Razer Opus ANC Wireless Headphones don’t look like a Razer product. Where’s the green? Where’s the RGB? Even the branding is subdued.

These headphones are a grown-up Razer product, probably meant to be headphones you can take anywhere and not stick out as a gamer.

The Midnight Blue color is a nice change from black. I have a few pairs of wireless headphones and every single pair is black, so I appreciate having a little variety. Midnight Blue is a very deep blue -- so deep it’s almost black.

I’ve been trying the Opus headphones out for a few weeks and they have become the headphones I use every day. Before, I was using the Sony XB900N.

My favorite thing about the Opus headphones is how comfortable they are. The headband and ear cups have cushy padding. The headphones don’t squeeze my head too tight and don’t weigh a lot. I can wear these for 5+ hours at a time and not get a headache.

Sound quality is decent. I mostly use the Opus for listening to music and TV/movies. Compared to Razer’s gaming headsets, this isn’t one I’d pick for serious gaming. There is a tiny bit of lag and the low, deep sounds aren’t as punchy as with say, a Razer Kraken headset.

Razer’s claim of up to 25 hours of battery life seems pretty accurate. I didn’t keep a log every time I used the headphones, but I was able to use them for 4-5 hours a day for a good week before needing to charge. Unfortunately there is no battery indicator on the headphones to know when the battery is running low.

I don’t love the Razer Opus app needed to tweak a few of the settings. I have an older Android phone running Nougat, the app is incompatible with my phone. So I had to borrow my mom’s iPhone to install the app. By default, the headphones shut off after 5 minutes and I could only change this setting in the app. The app also allows you to switch between a few audio presets (but you can’t create your own) and check battery life.

If I take the headphones off my head, they automatically pause whatever I’m watching or listening to. I like this; my mom often talks to me when I’m wearing headphones, so it’s a lot quicker to just take them off and now I don’t have to manually pause. This is a setting that can be changed in the app.

The Active Noise Cancelling is what I expect for a pair of headphones in this price range. It’s decent. Not great, not horrible, but good enough to mute most background noise. But I don’t like that there’s not a light or indicator on the headphones to tell when I have ANC turned on.

The Opus doesn’t support Bluetooth multipoint.

The headphones charge via USB-C. The included case stores the headphones, charging cable, USB-C to USB A adapter, 3.5 mm audio cable, and airline adapter. The case actually has an outline on the bottom to tell you how to fit the headphones inside.
text_fidelity_b: Razer Opus Active Noise Cancelling ANC Wireless Headphones: THX Audio Tuning - 25 Hr Battery - Bluetooth 4.2 & 3.5mm Jack Compatible - Auto Play/Auto Pause - Carrying Case Included - Midnight Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100 The mouse functions fine and I do like the form of it. There is one critical problem though. The form forces the forward and back buttons to be on the opposite side of left and right click so while your thumb is on the forward or back, you have no choice but to squeeze the right or left click to engage the forward/back button. Obviously, this causes inadvertent clicks with the mouse which is a problem. It happens mainly on the forward button as this is where the left and right click start to engage, too (more forward on the mouse itself).

I have not decided if I will keep it or not as I rely heavily on the use of these buttons. If I can find a way to grip it so this does not occur, it will be fine. In the meantime, I'll be using it look for a mouse that is designed better.

UPDATE 2-23-16: Like many others who have posted less than favorable reviews, Anker customer support has reached out to me directly, twice, offering a full refund, which I declined. In my opinion, the mouse works well for it's price, but I stand by the issue noted above. I have gotten used to is and can grip the mouse slightly differently when using the forward button. For this reason and for the outstanding customer service, I have bumped the review to 3 stars and wouldn't hesitate to recommend trying it out given the extremely low risk.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Ergonomic Optical USB Wired Vertical Mouse 1000/1600 DPI, 5 Buttons CE100

(Discontinued) HP ENVY 32-Inch Screen LED-Lit Monitor Quad-HD There's a lot to like about this monitor, but also some clear drawbacks. Let's start with the good news.

In typical HP fashion it comes very well packaged to survive pretty much any measure of rough handling in transit. There's a "quick start" guide that is taped to the front of the monitor that walks you through the setup (which is very straightforward). There's also an excellent user guide in PDF on the included disk.

The overall design is very attractive. It's very slim, lightweight and easy to position. I'm using it with the included table stand since my wall-mount options can't handle a monitor this large (it does come with a metal plate with VESA-compatible holes should you want to use it with a mount).

I used this on both a PC and as a video monitor hooked up through my AV receiver. For both situations I used the HDMI interface.

The sound quality is very good compared with the typical built-in speaker. It lacks bass "punch" but is quite acceptable.

Now for the so-so news: picture quality. It's good, but not "wow" good. Picture quality was somewhat drab looking, lacking crispness and contrast despite spending a lot of time tweaking the video quality with the many options available. It becomes worse when viewed off center (although it does have a decent viewing angle).

It comes with a remote which could be very handy for switching inputs, tweaking the picture, adjusting the sound, etc. I say it "could be" since the remote it comes with is horrible. It's small, which is good, but all the buttons are flush mount and have black on black lettering. It is very, very hard to see which button is which even in bright light. Forget about finding the right button in dim light. Truly horrible design work.

Netvue Indoor Camera, Enhanced Security Camera with Advanced AI Skills for Pet/Baby/Nanny, 1080P FHD 2.4GHz WiFi Night Vision Home Camera, 2-Way Audio Dog Camera Cloud Storage/TF Card, Black This is the third Netvue Camera I purchased. At the time of this review, this Netvue Orb Cam is the same list price as the Netvue Home Cam I previously purchased. Taking into consideration that Netvue Home Cam doesn't have the Pan & Tilt feature that this Cam does, getting added features for the same price is always nice.

Linking this camera to my account was straightforward and easy to do. Also, setup was easier to do than most wifi plugs and wall switches.

My son added my Netvue cameras to my Alexa account and setup Routines so the motion detection turns on lights connected to smart plugs as I walk through the house.

Performance of this Camera matches the quality of my other Netvue Cams and my Ring Doorbell 2 cam.

Pan & Tilt feature is sluggish and does not allow for small adjustment. For me that's not a problem because I won't be changing its angle or position regularly.

As seen in the attached photo, my son installed it at the edge of a window so that the anchor screws went into a stud and the camera wire could be hidden behind a curtain. He moved the surge protector that my cell phone charger and clock plugs into and mounted it on the wall so the camera could be plugged in as it was not long enough to reach the electrical outlet. We had to move furniture around to hide the surge protector.

NOTES:
TO PET OWNERS, if this camera not mounted and is set on a bookcase, the Pan & Tilt feature will not angle down below the level of the item it is sitting on, which means you may not see your pet walking around. I have a German Shepard as a service dog (mobility dog) and I mounted my camera on the wall so I could always see him.

Standard house door is roughly 80" (6' 8") and most home ceiling heights are 8 ft (96") but sometimes 10ft or 12ft. The power cords on all 3 Netvue cameras I own are 6ft (same as a standard household item such as a fan or clock). Every camera has required an extension cord and moving furniture.

I have have read numerous reviews about Smart Home devices complaining they are only 2.4g. 5.0g Wifi has faster transfer speeds but lower reception distances. 2.4g, like this device has, is more reliable with less connection interruptions.
text_fidelity_b: Netvue Indoor Camera, Enhanced Security Camera with Advanced AI Skills for Pet/Baby/Nanny, 1080P FHD 2.4GHz WiFi Night Vision Home Camera, 2-Way Audio Dog Camera Cloud Storage/TF Card, Black

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS C100PA-DB02 10.1-inch Touch Chromebook Flip (1.8GHz, 4GB Memory, 16GB eMMC, Google OS), All Metal Body Writing this from this very Chromebook a couple months after I got it. I have a nice desktop PC, gaming laptop, Android tablet, Nexus phone, but this is my most-used device. It's small, light, fast, and the screen is great.
Battery lasts between 5-8 hours depending what you are doing with it. I usually listen to podcasts, browse the web, and watch Youtube and Netflix.
I don't have any complaints about this device. I knew what I was buying beforehand, and what I would have access to with just Chrome OS. I frequently access documents through Google Drive and have had no problems opening any of the typical document formats. Video plays well on Youtube and Netflix.
I love, love, LOVE the replacement function keys on this. Since it's a pared-down OS, the typical Windows F1, F2 etc. keys are removed. You instead have back, forward, refresh, fullscreen, multiple windows, brightness and volume keys set as the topmost keys. They are incredibly handy and make it feel like a lightweight "browsing/media" device.
I was tired of hauling my gaming laptop around the house and wished my tablet and phone had a keyboard, so this was the perfect solution.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS C100PA-DB02 10.1-inch Touch Chromebook Flip (1.8GHz, 4GB Memory, 16GB eMMC, Google OS), All Metal Body

It was expensive, a little overpriced, in my opinion.

text_fidelity_a:
Sonpre Samurai Max-C Pop-up SD Rechargeable Speaker for Smartphones/Laptops/Tablets/MP3s - Black This is a more upscale version of the “pop up” speakers that have been around for a while. It adds some useful features including an SD card slot to play mp3 files directly and more advanced controls, such as a toggle switch for track skip and a mute button.

When compressed it’s very compact, measuring roughly 2.5 inches in diameter. While it can be played in its compact mode, the sound quality is not all that great – very tinny with little bass.

The sound quality improves significantly when it’s popped open. That increases the height to about 3.25 inches. That doesn't seem like much, but it makes a huge difference in sound quality. The bass is far more pronounced and, while the mid and upper ranges are still somewhat muddy, it’s far more pleasant to listen to than when it is folded up.

Given the size, I’d rate the sound quality as very good when it is in its pop-up mode. This is not a room-filling speaker but it sounds a whole lot better than the internal speakers in a tablet.

It is a direct-connect only speaker – it does NOT have bluetooth. It comes with a 3.5mm cord that is permanently attached to the base of the speaker. The cable can be stowed in a grove on the base of the speaker. The attached cable is a plus and a minus: you’ll never forget to bring a cable along, but the cord is only about 5 inches long, which made it backward to use on some of my equipment. I like that the cord is attached, but it really needs to be a bit longer.

The build quality feels pretty solid. It’s all plastic, as expected, but it has a nice feel to it. The bellows section in the middle feels like it is build solid enough to last a while. Plus, the fact that you can close it up easily for transport gives me some measure of assurance that it will survive being tossed around a bit. For the price, I’d rate the build quality as very good.

There are less expensive pop-up speakers available, such as the Xboom. I have one of those as well, and when comparing the two side-by-side I thought the sound quality was bit better on the Sonpre. The Sonpre also has more features than the Xboom (the mute button in particular is a welcome addition) and has longer battery life. So, while it is a few bucks more, it does bring some additional features to the table.

Although the short cord drops my rating by a star, this is definitely one to consider if you’re looking for a decent sounding pop-up speaker.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Sonpre Samurai Max-C Pop-up SD Rechargeable Speaker for Smartphones/Laptops/Tablets/MP3s - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Pangea Audio Vulcan TT Turntable Stand with Vinyl Record Storage - Black Some appear to have had some difficulty or confusion with assembly, but I did it solo fairly quickly with no issues and found the instructions very clear. No tools were needed and all of the pieces went on smoothly. The direction sheet clearly shows and lists what pieces to use. I guess some didn’t see that one of the shelf sections is thicker. The stand appears quite sturdy and stable. Yes, the only real issue is if you’re using the discs at the feet. I guess the bare, spike type feet ends are supposed to be for thick carpet. Like many I had mine on wood/laminate flooring and so need the small discs as the spike tips will surely scratch it up. This isn’t really a problem per se, but it is quite finicky and it the only part of the operation my wife had to assist with. It definitely would’ve been nice if they’d just included both a spike and attached foot type tips with the stand especially at this price. I included two pics with this review that I took while in the process of getting it and components situated. The stand easily fits my vintage Sansui 661 receiver on the middle shelf and Audio Technica LP120 turntable on the top. I hope both this review and photos showing it with the perspective of having components on it help.

Edit: So, yea, I did dock a star due to the feet issue. As I noted they are finicky, but can quickly get frustrating. While I had to move the stand around getting my stereo stuff sorted the small discs constantly came off and you just really can’t put them back in solo. They will and did put small indentations on my floor with the discs off. My solution was to pick up a 4 pack of 1” sliders from WM that are plastic on the bottom with an adhesive disc on the top. I then stuck the small metal discs from the stand on the slider. Once my wife helped me place the discs back on the legs it could then slide pretty freely and they stayed on. text_fidelity_a: Seagate Barracuda 7200 1 TB 7200RPM SATA 3Gb/s 32MB Cache 3.5 Inch Internal Hard Drive I'd give it negative 5 if I could. I was working on my computer one night. It froze.  I walked the dog.... came back. Still frozen. Reboot. No Operating system. Seatools said bad LBAs.  Then that died. Couldn't even get bad LBAs.  So I take the circuit board off and send it to be replaced with a new board, my chip. Put it in the computer. Computer sees it the CCxx version and all, but freezes and won't boot.  Walked the dog, came back, still nothing. So I buy a kit that communicates through the serial connection of the drive. Nothing. Won't read, won't write. How do I know. I thought I had backed up my drive but when I looked at the files saved on my back up drive, it had not saved anything for a year.  I had been noticing it freezes when I am trying to copy to a back up drive.  The thing that drives me crazy is it comes on and seems to work but won't do anything.  When I tried to format it, the computer shows the drive size in the format window, but says it can't format it. When I put it in a USB drive, windows recognized it was there but thinks it is 0 bytes.  I would never have bought a seagate in the first place but it came in a computer I purchased already built.  I used to make my own but thought it was cheaper to just buy. I got cheaper alright.

text_fidelity_a:
FYHXele Computer Monitor, Gaming Monitor 24 Inch 75Hz, IPS FHD 1080P, 2xHDMI, USB Type-C, Built-in Speakers, Adaptive Sync, VESA for Office Home, Black I’ve been using the FYHXele 24 Inch Monitor (75Hz version) for the last month, and it has totally spoiled me for playing games on my Switch! The monitor has built-in speakers, so I can hear a game’s music while playing. It’s a small but nice feature; I can easily switch the input from my laptop to my Switch and not have to rearrange my whole desk to play games.

The picture is bright and vibrant. I’ve been playing Hades for the last month and it looks SO good on this screen. Bright and crisp, even if I play during the day. I also use the monitor as a second display for work, it’s good for that too, either as a streaming display or for text and spreadsheets.

I use it with my MacBook Pro, the monitor has 2 HDMI inputs and 1 USB-C. The USB-C port doesn’t support passthrough charging.

A VESA plate is included, which was a nice plus. I do use a monitor arm because I don’t like the stand this monitor comes with. The angle and height are not adjustable at all, and I didn’t like the default angle. The base is 9 inches by 7 inches, so it has a large footprint. I also don’t love the “FYHXele” printed in white at the bottom of the screen.

The power cable is relatively short, only 50 inches. It’s an AC adapter, not a power brick. The box also includes an HDMI cable -- another nice plus -- but unfortunately my cable had a cut in the coating, so I could see the copper wire.

Overall, I think this is a decent budget monitor. I never want to play my Switch in handheld mode anymore, the picture quality has spoiled me that much. The dual HDMI inputs make it easy to switch between work and fun; I’ve also used this as a Discord display, rotated 90° on a VESA arm.
text_fidelity_b: FYHXele Computer Monitor, Gaming Monitor 24 Inch 75Hz, IPS FHD 1080P, 2xHDMI, USB Type-C, Built-in Speakers, Adaptive Sync, VESA for Office Home, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Byron Statics Portable CD Boombox with AM/FM Radio, Top Loading CD, 1W RMS x 2 Stereo Speaker, Aux-in Jack, LCD Display, AC110-120V Operated (KBB-250) I’m old enough to remember the old 8-track players, but growing up my media player was of course a cassette player, and sometimes a “dual” player.

But, in 1995, I opted to transition to CDs. By that time they were a bit more affordable, though the average $17.95 felt like it was anything but.

By around 2005, I was transitioning to an MP3 player. The first one was a literal BRICK (Creative Nomad).

And, by 2008, I had an iPod Nano. By 2011, I had the iPod classic. Even my 2008 Chevy had an aux port to connect my iPod to. So, I really had NO need of a CD player. After all, most of my music was on my computer or iPod. Living in an apartment is NOT ideal for a “stereo”. I wouldn’t want to hear someone else’s music, so I don’t think they’d want to hear mine.

When I saw this, I decided to get it.

It is COMPACT, no frills, no remote control. In fact there is only a “selection” button, not a (back track or forward track).

I haven’t tried the radio function yet. The CD top loader consists of a manual opening (no push-button), and the CD has to be popped in and out manually. The sound is pretty decent for the size of the unit. This is more for desktop or bedside use. Definitely not for a home “sound system”.

I then tested the AUX cable for the iPod and the sound was the same as the CD. That feature was REALLY easy to use.

It is a pretty solid, light-weight unit. I do believe it could be a bit cheaper. I wouldn’t mind getting a second one should the price drop.
text_fidelity_b: Byron Statics Portable CD Boombox with AM/FM Radio, Top Loading CD, 1W RMS x 2 Stereo Speaker, Aux-in Jack, LCD Display, AC110-120V Operated (KBB-250)

text_fidelity_a:
NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green) Although there are a lot of positive points to be said about this product, a major flaw with it is that - even on low volumes and on songs without much bass - you can hear a bit of distortion, like crackly static, that sounds like a speaker that you're either working too hard or is at the end of its life. This becomes worse as the battery gets low. I consider this issue to be "understandable and sort of acceptable" considering the whole system has to run on battery power and most people aren't expecting high power out of such a setup. They might just have a high-pass crossover set too high to conserve power, and too much is cut off, resulting in messy sound.

When you charge your phone with the speaker's battery (which in itself is sort of a nice, if cannibalistic, feature, one that other devices claim even though it is inherent to the device; with this, the USB-A port was added specifically for this purpose), it lowers the volume to level 8 (there is nothing to tell you what level you're at) to keep from draining the battery quickly. Even at this medium level and below, this problem can be recognized.

The bike mounts are 4" apart, center to center, so make sure you have room on your bike handlebars if that is your purpose for ordering. Included bike mounts are good. It also comes with a neoprene case, a USB cable, and an audio cable, both red. With all these extras trying to give the appearance of premium, it doesn't actually come with a charger, not that this will be an issue for most people (you probably already have more than you know what to do with).

There should be keyhole slots built into the bike mounts so it could also be hung on the wall and removed easily, making it more versatile.

The unit pairs easily and immediately with my Blackberry every time, and it can control the tracks through the BT connection as well. It looks well made and has a good feel to it. It looks like it could almost be waterproof, although I noticed no mention or claim of that feature (so I'm sure it's not).

The sound overall isn't bad for a low voltage battery operated speaker, as long as you're not sitting down and listening too closely. I guess for the purposes of making noise as you ride around the neighborhood, it'll do just fine.
text_fidelity_b: NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green)
